No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (D). The sentence is grammatically correct as written.

Rule/Concept: Nouns ending in -s but Singular in Meaning Certain nouns in English are plural in form (they end in -s) but are strictly singular in meaning and function. Because they represent a single unit or concept, they must be followed by a singular verb to maintain subject-verb agreement.

Nouns that follow this pattern: Gallows, News, Summons, Ethics, Physics, Mathematics, Economics, Billiards, Measles, Mumps.

options_en: The ancient texts, which have been meticulously preserved by the monks for centuries,
regarded the sun the primary source of all life and energy on the earth
despite the limited astronomical instruments available to the scholars of that era.
No Error
options_hi: The ancient texts, which have been meticulously preserved by the monks for centuries,
regarded the sun the primary source of all life and energy on the earth
despite the limited astronomical instruments available to the scholars of that era.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “the sun the” with “the sun as the”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Mandatory Use of "As" with Specific Verbs -

Certain verbs must be followed by the preposition "as" when they are used to define or describe the complement of an object. These verbs include: Regard, Describe, View, Know, Define, Treat, Characterize.

💢 Application to the Given Question - The verb "regarded" belongs to the category of verbs that require "as" to link the object ("the sun") with its description ("the primary source"). Without "as", the sentence becomes grammatically incomplete and structurally weak.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I have always regarded him as my brother.

Example 2: The biologist described the specimen as a new species of fungi.

Example 3: He defined success as the ability to overcome repeated failures.

NOTE: Conversely, verbs like Name, Elect, Think, Consider, Call, Choose, Make, and Appoint should NOT be followed by "as".

Things to Remember / Exam Tips -

The "Consider" Trap: This is the most common confusion in SSC exams. Consider does not take "as" (e.g., "I consider him my mentor" ✅), but Regard must take "as".

The "Known" Rule: If you use "Known", always check for "as" (e.g., "He is known as the father of chemistry").

Memory Hack: Think of "R-D-V" (Regard, Describe, View). These three are the most frequently tested verbs requiring "as" in CGL Mains

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: After the severe hailstorm damaged the
warehouse roof, the manager got the entire
structure repair by a team of specialized contractors.
No Error
options_hi: After the severe hailstorm damaged the
warehouse roof, the manager got the entire
structure repair by a team of specialized contractors.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (C) Replace “repair” with “repaired”.

📌 Rule / Concept: The Causative Passive

Sub + get/have + object + past participle + by + real doer

When we use verbs like Have or Get to show that someone else performed a task for us, the grammar depends entirely on what follows the verb. If a thing/object (the receiver) comes first, we must use the Past Participle (V3).

The Logic:

  • Active: The manager got the contractors (People) to repair the roof.

  • Passive: The manager got the roof (Object) repaired.

In the passive version, we don't care who did it as much as what was done to the object.

💢 Application to the Given Question

The sentence is designed to overwhelm you with descriptive clauses ("After the severe hailstorm," "team of specialized contractors"), but the core error is found in the causative link:

"...got the entire structure (Object) repair (Incorrect Verb Form)..."

  1. The Causative Verb: "Got"

  2. The Object: "The entire structure" (The warehouse roof/building).

  3. The Action: "Repair."

Since the "structure" cannot repair itself, the relationship is passive. the verb "repair" must be changed to its third form, "repaired."

Corrected sentence

After the severe hailstorm damaged the warehouse roof, the manager got the entire structure repaired by a team of specialized contractors.

More Examples for Clarity

  • Example 1: I had my hair cut yesterday. (Not cutted or to cut).

  • Example 2: She got her laptop fixed at the service center. (Not fix).

  • Example 3: You should have your eyes tested regularly. (Not test).

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: Under no circumstances the security personnel are permitted
to allow unauthorized visitors into the high-security server room
without a valid biometric clearance and prior written authorization.
No Error
options_hi: Under no circumstances the security personnel are permitted
to allow unauthorized visitors into the high-security server room
without a valid biometric clearance and prior written authorization.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) Replace “the security personnel are” with “are the security personnel”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Inversion with Negative Adverbial Phrases

When a sentence begins with a restrictive or negative adverbial phrase such as Under no circumstances, At no time, In no way, On no account, or On no condition, the sentence must follow the rule of Partial Inversion. This means the auxiliary verb (is, are, was, were, do, does, did, has, have, had, or modals like should/will) must be placed before the subject.

💢 Application to the Given Question

Under no circumstances the security personnel are permitted...

In the sentence above, the phrase "Under no circumstances" is a strong negative restriction placed at the beginning for emphasis. Therefore, the subject "the security personnel" cannot be followed by the verb "are". The auxiliary verb "are" must be moved before the subject to satisfy the inversion requirement.

Corrected Sentence

Under no circumstances are the security personnel permitted to allow unauthorized visitors into the high-security server room without a valid biometric clearance and prior written authorization.

More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅: At no time did the suspect admit to being present at the crime scene.

Example 2 ✅: On no account must you disclose the password to anyone, including bank officials.

Example 3 ✅: In no way does this minor setback affect our long-term growth strategy.

appeal remain remarkably intact.
No Error
options_hi: Although the architectural marvel is centuries
old, it’s structural integrity and aesthetic
appeal remain remarkably intact.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “it’s” with “its”.

Rule / Concept: Its vs. It's

In this sentence, we are referring to the integrity belonging to the architectural marvel. We need the possessive form. If we use "it’s", the sentence translates to: "...centuries old, it is structural integrity...", which is logically and grammatically nonsensical. Therefore, we must use the possessive "its".

questions.q_en: One should adhere strictly to ethical standards in public office, ______?
questions.q_hi: One should adhere strictly to ethical standards in public office, ______?
options_en: shouldn’t one
shouldn’t he
doesn’t one
don’t they
options_hi: shouldn’t one
shouldn’t he
doesn’t one
don’t they
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) - “shouldn’t one”.

📌 Rule / Concept: “One” Pronoun Agreement in Question Tags

When the subject of a sentence is “one” (used in a general sense), the question tag must also use “one”, not “he” or “they”.

The pronoun in the tag must match the subject of the main clause.

💢 Application to the Given Question -

  • Subject = one

  • Modal verb = should

  • Statement is positive → tag must be negative

  • Pronoun must remain one

Therefore: shouldn’t one?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅- One must respect constitutional values, mustn’t one?

Example 2 ✅ - One cannot ignore procedural fairness, can one?

Example 3 ✅ - One ought to verify the facts, oughtn’t one?

🧠 Things to Remember

  • “One” → repeat “one” in the tag.

  • Never replace it with “he” in exam.

  • Modal verb in main clause → same modal in tag.

questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The senior manager expressed his deep dissatisfaction because the junior consultants
are always coming up with innovative yet highly impractical solutions
that do not align with the budgetary constraints of our prestigious clients.
No Error
options_hi: The senior manager expressed his deep dissatisfaction because the junior consultants
are always coming up with innovative yet highly impractical solutions
that do not align with the budgetary constraints of our prestigious clients.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (D) - No Error.

📌 Rule / Concept: Present Continuous with "Always" for Annoyance -

While the Present Continuous tense is typically used for actions happening at the moment of speaking, it is paired with adverbs of frequency like "always," "forever," or "constantly" to express a persistent habit, especially one that is annoying, surprising, or occurs more frequently than expected. In high-level exams, this is often tested to see if a student mistakenly thinks "always" can only be used with the Simple Present tense for routine facts.

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the senior manager is expressing dissatisfaction. The use of "are always coming up" (Present Continuous) correctly conveys that this is a repetitive, irritating habit of the junior consultants. If the sentence used the simple present "always come up," it would sound like a neutral statement of fact rather than a grievance. Since the structure $Subject + is/am/are + always + V1+ing$ is perfectly applied here to show a frequent, annoying action, there is no grammatical error.

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: She is always losing her car keys just when we are about to leave the house. (Expresses annoyance) ✅

Example 2: My brother is constantly interrupting me when I am on a professional Zoom call. (Expresses a frequent, irritating habit) ✅

Example 3: You are forever complaining about the weather instead of enjoying the vacation. (Expresses a persistent negative habit) ✅

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is - Option (B).

Replace “runner-ups” with “runners-up”.

Rule/Concept: Pluralization of Compound Nouns -

-A compound noun is a noun made up of two or more words. To make a compound noun plural, we must identify the root word (the principal or main word) and add 's' to it.

-In the word "runner-up," the main noun is "runner," while "up" is a preposition acting as a modifier. Therefore, the plural form is "runners-up ✅," not "runner-ups. ❌"

Corrected Sentence - The state government has appointed several runners-up of the national sports meet as junior athletic coaches.

More Examples for Clarity -

-All my sons-in-law are professionally successful. ✅

-The hangers-on were waiting outside the celebrity's house. ✅

-Many passers-by witnessed the unusual phenomenon. ✅

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

-Identify the Headword: Always ask "Who or what is the main thing?" In Member of Parliament, "Member" is the headword (Members of Parliament).

-The Preposition Trap: Words ending in in-law, by, on, up usually take the 's' on the first word.

questions.solution_en:

Rule / Concept: Two Nouns referring to Different Persons –

When two or more nouns in a sentence refer to different persons, the definite article 'the' must be used before each noun. The most reliable way to identify this in an exam is to look at the verb; a plural verb indicates that the nouns represent distinct individuals.

Things to Remember / Exam Tips-

The Verb is the Key: Always check the verb (is/was vs. are/were) first. It acts as the signal for how many articles are needed.

Pronoun Agreement: If the sentence uses a plural possessive like 'their', it is a strong hint that you are dealing with two separate individuals requiring two articles.

options_en: Many philosophers throughout history have spent their lives trying to
wander about the true nature of human consciousness and the
fundamental purpose of existence in an seemingly indifferent universe.
No Error
options_hi: Many philosophers throughout history have spent their lives trying to
wander about the true nature of human consciousness and the
fundamental purpose of existence in an seemingly indifferent universe.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “wander” with “wonder”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Wonder vs. Wander -

These two words are frequently confused due to their similar spelling and sound, but they belong to different semantic categories:

Wonder (Verb/Noun): To feel curiosity, doubt, or surprise. It is a mental activity. (e.g., "I wonder why he is late.")

Wander (Verb): To move about aimlessly, stray from a path, or roam. It is a physical activity. (e.g., "The cattle wandered into the field.")

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the context involves philosophers contemplating and questioning the nature of existence. This is a cognitive/mental process, not a physical movement. Therefore, the verb wonder (to think/query) must be used instead of "wander" (to roam).

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I wonder if it will rain today.

Example 2: We wandered through the narrow streets of the old city.

Example 3: Her mind began to wander during the long and boring lecture. (Note: This is a metaphorical use of 'wander' for thoughts moving away from a topic.)

When I visited the village, I made sure to __________ my elderly neighbor who had been unwell for weeks.
options_en: ask for
ask about
ask after
ask over
options_hi: ask for
ask about
ask after
ask over
questions.solution_en:
Explanation: The correct answer is option (3).

English Explanation: “Ask after” means to inquire about someone’s health or well-being, especially in a caring or polite way. In the sentence, the speaker visited the village and wanted to check on the elderly neighbor who had been unwell. Therefore, “ask after” correctly conveys the idea of inquiring about someone’s condition. “Ask for” means to request something. “Ask about” means to seek information about something in general. “Ask over” means to invite someone to come to your home. Since the context involves politely inquiring about someone’s health, “ask after” is the most appropriate fit.

1. Ask for (मांग करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी वस्तु या सहायता की मांग करना।
Example: She asked for a glass of water. (उसने एक गिलास पानी मांगा।)

2. Ask about (के बारे में पूछना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी विषय के बारे में जानकारी लेना।
Example: He asked about the new policy. (उसने नई नीति के बारे में पूछा।)

3. Ask after (कुशलक्षेम पूछना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी की सेहत या हालचाल पूछना।
Example 1: The teacher asked after the student who had been absent due to illness. (शिक्षक ने बीमारी के कारण अनुपस्थित छात्र की कुशलक्षेम पूछी।)
Example 2: She always asks after her grandparents during phone calls. (वह फोन पर हमेशा अपने दादा-दादी की कुशलक्षेम पूछती है।)

4. Ask over (घर बुलाना / आमंत्रित करना)
Meaning in Hindi: किसी को घर आने के लिए आमंत्रित करना।
Example: We asked them over for dinner last night. (हमने उन्हें कल रात खाने पर बुलाया।)

    • Option A incorrectly changes the tense to Simple Past.

    • Option C incorrectly changes the reporting verb from "will say" to "would say."

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: In the far corner of the dusty, abandoned library
was several rare manuscripts containing the lost
botanical records of the Victorian-era exploratory expeditions.
No Error
options_hi: In the far corner of the dusty, abandoned library
was several rare manuscripts containing the lost
botanical records of the Victorian-era exploratory expeditions.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) Replace “was” with “were”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Full Inversion with Adverbials of Place

When a sentence begins with a Prepositional Phrase of Place (In the corner, On the table, Under the bridge), and the main verb is a verb of state, position, or existence (be, stand, sit, lie, exist), the sentence undergoes Full Inversion.

In this structure, the entire verb or verb phrase comes before the subject. The most common error in competitive exams is "Subject-Verb Agreement." The verb must agree with the subject that follows it, not the noun inside the prepositional phrase.

💢 Application to the Given Question

In the far corner of the dusty, abandoned library was several rare manuscripts...

In this sentence, the phrase "In the far corner of the dusty, abandoned library" is the adverbial of place. The real subject of the sentence is "several rare manuscripts," which is plural. Therefore, using the singular auxiliary verb "was" is grammatically incorrect. It must be changed to the plural form "were" to match the subject

Corrected Sentence

In the far corner of the dusty, abandoned library were several rare manuscripts containing the lost botanical records of the Victorian-era exploratory expeditions.

The professor said to the class, "Why did you forget that water boils at 100°C?"
questions.q_hi:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.

The professor said to the class, "Why did you forget that water boils at 100°C?"
options_en: The professor asked the class why they had forgotten that water boiled at 100°C.
The professor asked the class why they forgot that water boils at 100°C.
The professor asked the class why they had forgotten that water boils at 100°C.
The professor asked the class that why they had forgotten that water boils at 100°C.
options_hi: The professor asked the class why they had forgotten that water boiled at 100°C.
The professor asked the class why they forgot that water boils at 100°C.
The professor asked the class why they had forgotten that water boils at 100°C.
The professor asked the class that why they had forgotten that water boils at 100°C.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option C: The professor asked the class why they had forgotten that water boils at 100°C.

Key Points

  • Reporting Verb & Type: The sentence is an interrogative (Wh- question), so "said to" changes to "asked".

  • No Conjunction "That": In "Wh-" questions, the question word ("why") acts as the connector. Option D is incorrect because it adds an unnecessary "that".

  • The Two-Tense Rule: This sentence has two parts that follow different rules:

    1. The Action ("Why did you forget"): This is a specific past action. Since the reporting verb "asked" is in the past, the Simple Past ("did forget") must backshift to Past Perfect ("had forgotten").

    2. The Fact ("water boils at 100°C"): This is a Scientific/Universal Truth. Even though it is inside a past tense narration, the tense does not change. It must remain "boils".

  • Pronoun Change: The second-person pronoun "you" refers to the "class" (plural), so it changes to "they".

  • Word Order: In indirect speech, the question becomes a statement, so the subject ("they") comes before the verb ("had forgotten").

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option B

👉 Replace the blank with “when”.

📌 Rule / Concept: Correlative Adverbs (Hardly/Scarcely... when)

In English grammar, certain negative or restrictive adverbs are used in pairs to denote that one action happened almost immediately after another. The adverbial phrases “Hardly,” “Scarcely,” and “Barely” are strictly followed by the conjunction “when” (or occasionally "before"), but never by "than" or "then."

Structure: Hardly + Auxiliary Verb + Subject + Main Verb ... when + Subject + Second Action.

Inversion: If the sentence starts with "Hardly," the auxiliary verb (usually had) must come before the subject.

✅ Corrected Sentence: I had hardly fallen asleep when the neighbor's dog started barking.

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1: Hardly had the thief seen the police when he started running.

Example 2: I had scarcely finished my meal when the doorbell rang.
